page.layout: Two printed columns of Latin text on the left page (the left column of the scan), with a parallel Greek column on the right side of the scan beside it; the Greek column carries letter marks A to F in the margin between the two columns. Below the Greek column a Greek line runs across the full width. Page number 928 at top left, running head ARISTOTELIS at top centre.

main_text.p: Natatus alteri retrorsum, alteri anteuersus in os agitur. Pariunt ea sui corporis parte, quæ fistula dicitur, qua & coire eas nonnulli arbitrantur.
main_text.head: CAPVT VII.
main_text.p: Genera crusta operta, vt locustæ, gammari, squillæ, & huiusmodi reliqua, more quadrupedum retro mingentium coeunt, scilicet vt fœmina caudam supinam exponat, mas suam superponat, & applicet. Coire solent ineunte vere iuxta terram. Iam enim coitus omnium id genus exploratus est. Interdum etiam cum ficus maturescunt, coire incipiunt. Hoc eodem modo gammari quoque, & squillæ coeunt. Cancri parte priore copulantur, sua opercula loculosa illa, rugosáque mutua confertione componentes. Primùm cancer minor ab auerso superueni-re solet, tum maior, vbi ille superuenerit, vertit se in latus. Nulla re differt fœmina à mare, nisi quòd operculum applicatile illud amplius, & distantius, & hirsutius fœminæ gerant, in quo oua pariunt, & quà egerunt excrementum. Membrum autem, quod mas in fœminam inserat, nullum omnino habetur.
main_text.head: CAPVT VIII.
main_text.p: Insecta auersa coeunt: deinde quod minus est, superuenit maius, hoc est, mas fœminam. Nec mas in fœminam genitale vllum inserit membrum more animalium cæterorum: sed fœmina sursum in maris receptum, caudæ vltimum suæ meatum quendam producens reflectit: qui in nonnullis maior, quàm proportione totius corporis esse videtur, cùm ipsa parua admodum sint. Sed sunt etiam, in quibus minus inconueniens æstimetur. Planum hoc fuerit, si musceas coitu venereo copulatas diuiseris. Tardo etiam, quæ coiuerint, seiunguntur digressu: diu nanque eorum copulatio durat: quod in iis, quæ in nostro conspectu versantur, facilè patet: verbi causa, in muscis, in scarabeis. Omnia enim ad hunc modum coeunt, videlicet muscæ, scarabei, verticilla, phalangia, & si quid aliud generis eiusdem coire solet. Phalangiis, quæ texunt, coitus agitur hoc modo: Cùm fœmina deducta aranea traxerit, mas eandem mutuò trahit: quod vbi sepius fecerint, coeunt, & auersis clunibus copulantur: nā propter aluum orbiculatam modus hic coniungendi iis congruit.

{A} Greek text of the parallel column (Aristotle, Historia animalium, Greek original) is transcribed in the Greek column; the Greek is printed on the right side of the scan and is not reproduced here in full.

page.notes: The right-hand column is printed in Greek (Aristotle's original, with the heading Κεφάλαιον ζ. and Κεφάλαιον η.), and the Greek line across the bottom is also Greek. Greek was not transcribed letter by letter; the Latin text and page furniture are given above. Letter marks A to F sit between the columns, and the marks B, C, D, E, F stand beside the Latin column. Possible doubtful readings: "Insecta" in the Latin heading area and "musceas" are as printed on the scan.
